function: p. 5-6, 9-10: over-the-air aggregation of CKKS-encrypted federated-learning updates through AirComp, with ciphertext-oriented homomorphic mapping and MIMO transmit/receive beamforming optimization.
system: p. 11: massive MIMO uplink, K=10 devices with Nt=8 antennas, server with Nr=64, i.i.d. Rayleigh fading, 25 dB SNR, 40 MHz bandwidth; carrier frequency not stated; no RIS.
method: p. 10-11: FedAvg federated training of LeNet, AlexNet and ResNet-20 on CKKS-encrypted updates; AirComp beamformers from non-learned column-wise BCD optimization.
data_channel: p. 11: simulated i.i.d. Rayleigh fading; MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for the FL task; network profile per ITU-R M.2135 (40 MHz, 2.36 bps/Hz).
test_conditions: p. 13-14: same datasets for training and testing; separate runs sweeping K, Nt, Nr, SNR and IID versus Dirichlet non-IID; no cross-setting test.
baselines: p. 11-12: naiveHEFed (digital orthogonal access, no optimization), EPFL [5] compression, FedPHE-PS [6] sparsification, and the HEAirFed-noHP ablation; no earlier AirComp transceiver design compared.
metrics: p. 12-15: test accuracy over iterations, normalized optimality gap, communication and aggregation latency, approximation error versus theory, decryption-correctness range.
complexity: p. 11: transceiver time complexity O(L Nt^2 Nr^2) per device column and O(L(Nt^2 Nr^2 + K Nr^2 Nt)) at the server; latencies in Table III (p. 14).
q1_support: p. 11: "(i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading [20], [41]" is a custom textbook simulator. p. 11: "The network is profiled based on ITU-R M.2135 standards" gives only bandwidth and spectral efficiency, not a channel model; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "across four datasets when fixing K = 10": the non-IID, K, Nt, Nr and SNR sweeps (pp. 12-14) are separate FL runs evaluated in their own setting; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 12: "EPFL: The state-of-art Compression-based optimization in CKKS-enabled FL [5]" and p. 12: "digital orthogonal multiple access techniques without any optimization in communication and aggregation latency suppression"; p. 12: "EPFL and FedPHE-PS exhibit lower accuracy" compares accuracy and latency (Figs. 4, 8).
q4_support: p. 11: "For parameter server, the time complexity for calculating both optimal A(j) and C (j) are O(L(Nt 2 Nr 2 + KNr 2 Nt ))" gives the transceiver design complexity; the device side is O(L Nt^2 Nr^2).
q5_support: p. 1: "supplementary downloadable material available at https://doi.org/10.1109/TMC.2025.3610887" holds proofs only (p. 7: "Detailed proof is provided in Appendix A of the supplemental material"); p. 11: "We implemented CKKS based on the HEAAN C++ source code [43]" is third-party code; data are MNIST/CIFAR plus a simulated channel.
notes: Included under the rule that in FL over the air the learned element is the model trained across devices (LeNet, AlexNet, ResNet-20); the AirComp beamformers are classical BCD, not learned. Area 7 because the paper solves over-the-air aggregation of encrypted updates (pp. 2-3). q3 rests on EPFL [5] and FedPHE-PS [6], earlier published digital HE-FL designs, with naiveHEFed as the non-AirComp reference; no earlier AirComp design is compared, so the reviewer should confirm. ITU-R M.2135 is cited only for the network profile, so q1 is 0. RIS appears only as future work (p. 15).
